scope: Read checkout-sized files in one source packet and retrieve Chief-requested evidence automatically after revocation.
riskAnalysis: Read only tracked files through the existing repository policy. Bound serialized output, preserve exact continuation and keep historical request serialization verifiable.

threatModel.assets: Preview credentials, private repository assets, truthful browser pass/failure evidence and exact qualified release identity.
threatModel.trustBoundaries: Detached browser route callbacks versus test runner failure/report persistence; intentional context/page teardown versus unexpected transport errors.
threatModel.abuseCases: Swallowed background failures, fabricated Browser success after transport errors, raw error/query/credential logging, error ledger overflow hiding failures, unexpected closure mistaken for authorized cancellation.
threatModel.mitigations: Nonthrowing callback abort, finite code/phase/scope/resource/method/category ledger, cumulative failure count beyond bounded details, exact explicit cleanup markers plus canonical closure classifier, pending callback drain and final assertions before durable report writes.

defects.rootCause: The existing 8000-byte excerpt ceiling split the checkout handler even though it fits in a single request.
defects.detectionGap: The live Chief exercise exposed a manual source handoff. The old fixture covered small line ranges.
defects.regression: Read the real checkout handler in one packet and reconstruct long UTF-8 and newline-boundary fixtures across continuation reads.
defects.historicalPrevention: Preserve existing range reads and both prior Chief request encodings for historical receipts.

rollback: Keep paid execution disabled and preserve065 failed Browser archive and successful5380 CI/37 Redis evidence. Ship only reviewed feature successors; on failure retain or restore the preceding qualified feature alias without Production/main changes.

negativePaths.malformed-response: Raw exception strings, URLs and query parameters never enter the ledger; only fixed categories/phase/origin/resource/method classes. Unexpected private response statuses still fail exact public200/private404 probes.
negativePaths.stale-state: Exact source, release pin and private-source identity unchanged; new hosted Browser artifacts must match the actual successor before any paid Chief operation.
negativePaths.concurrency: Existing Browser workflow concurrency remains single per feature branch; this helper grants no concurrent provider execution or mutation rights.
negativePaths.cancellation: Explicit context/page teardown markers allow only canonical Playwright closure errors; unexpected closure and generic cancellation/socket/timeout remain failures. Marker never clears prior errors.
negativePaths.worker-interruption: Close drains all pending route callbacks. Unexpected failures prevent ok and persist safe diagnostics before final throw; no detached route exception can terminate report writing.
negativePaths.api-outage: HTTP401/403/200 at private paths cannot masquerade as private404; public positive control must200, all probes same-origin and exact path.
negativePaths.authorization-denial: Private header types stripped off-origin; same-origin separate fetch cannot follow redirects; browser carries no global custom credential headers.
negativePaths.spending-limit: No OpenAI or Sandbox requests in local security tests; owner-directed existing financial monitoring and uncertainty unchanged; no new paid resources.
negativePaths.partial-execution: Cumulative failure count remains authoritative beyond20 retained details; all tracked contexts are asserted after close, including helper contexts closed early. Preserve original hosted failure evidence.

proactiveReview.architecture: Extend the existing shared Preview access helper only; all six QA callers share explicit context/page close and final assertion. No provider gateway, executor, permission expansion or new orchestration.
proactiveReview.dependencies: Existing Playwright browser and Node APIs only, no packages or providers added. Actual proof uses isolated localhost fictional credentials, not personal browser state.
proactiveReview.threats: Cross-origin redirect forwarding is demonstrated with fictional credentials and eliminated by separate non-following request/fulfill, not by disabling protection.
proactiveReview.failureModes: Independent local Chrome reproduced context-close and socket failures with identical generic wrapper error; expected markers distinguish them while the exact original hosted cause remains unproven.
proactiveReview.faultInjection: Marked and unmarked closure, socket hangup, timeout, raw error containing fictional credential,25 failures with20 retained details, pending callbacks, foreign redirect and hypothetical credential types.
proactiveReview.independentChallenge: Existing independent Work QA exercises actual imported helper in real headless browser; Engineering Auditor separately reviews every active caller and diagnostics.
proactiveReview.recovery: Preserve current66c and original failed artifacts; one reviewed feature source push/build, durable alias marker/readback once READY, no configuration refresh or credential rewrite.
proactiveReview.readiness: 32 focused reader/controller checks and 139 UI checks passed, including complete checkout evidence and fenced automatic source retrieval. Hosted and live verification pending.
